kevin: Heads up — after rolling gpu-operator to v1.6.0 in eu-west-1 I'm seeing a bunch of training pods stuck in ContainerCreating. Not a full outage but ~18% of GPU pods can't schedule.

priya: Which nodes? any common kernel/driver mismatch in the node labels?

kevin: Mostly g4dn and p4d-ish pools. Sample kubelet log: 
```
Mar 12 09:14:22 node-az1 kubelet[1234]: Failed to start container "training": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to setup device plugin: driver not loaded (module version mismatch)
Mar 12 09:14:22 node-az1 kernel: nvidia: loaded module but kernel driver version 535.86 != nvidia-smi reported 535.54
```

mei: We saw a similar pattern in us-west-2 last quarter when the device-plugin started mounting /var/lib/nvidia differently. Can you `kubectl describe node` the allocatable GPUs?

kevin: `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu` shows GPUs present but `kubectl describe node node-az1` shows `nvidia.com/gpu: 0/1 allocatable` even though `nvidia-smi` on the host shows GPUs visible.

lucas: That smells like driver kernel module mismatch + kubelet/device-plugin handshake failing. The new plugin version also changed the socket path (maybe `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins_registry` vs `/var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins`) — some nodes still have the old symlink.

carla: infra-bot reported autoscaler churn in eu-west-1 after pods failed to schedule, we got temporary capacity spike and a cost blip. 

infra-bot: ALERT: GPU allocatable capacity in eu-west-1 down 18% (past 30m). Impacting namespaces: ml-prod, training.

priya: Any NCCL errors observed from the job logs? Different driver versions can introduce NCCL runtime comm failures.

kevin: Yes, here's snippet from a Horovod job: 
```
NCCL WARN Call to cuGetProcAddress failed, returned 217
NCCL ERROR Unhandled system error
```
Looks like runtime/device mismatch.

mei: Two quick paths: 1) revert gpu-operator to last known good (v1.5.x) which will restore old device-plugin behavior; 2) patch nodes by installing matching driver kernel module (535.86 vs 535.54) and restart kubelet/device-plugin. Revert buys time but blocks new operator features.

lucas: For production we should do a rolling driver alignment rather than revert the operator. Plan: cordon -> drain -> run driver install daemonset/ssh script -> reboot if module needs reload -> uncordon. Canary on 2 nodes per AZ first. Also update gpu-operator CR to enable `spec.driver.enabled: true` so operator manages drivers during rollout.

carla: Suggested commands for canary (one-liners):
```
kubectl cordon node-canary-1 && kubectl drain node-canary-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
helm upgrade gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator -f values-canary.yaml --set driver.enabled=true
kubectl apply -f driver-install-daemonset.yaml
# monitor: kubectl logs -n gpu-operator daemonset/driver-installer -f
```

kevin: Temporary safety/workaround if teams need immediate capacity: taint the affected nodes so batch jobs avoid them and shift steady-state production to unaffected pools. Example: `kubectl taint nodes node-az1 gpu-problem=true:NoSchedule`

priya: We should also check kernel versions across clouds — some older kernels refuse unsigned modules and the new driver packages changed signing. If we need to avoid reboots, `modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia` might work but only if versions match.

devops-bot: NOTE: Patch release policy: if rolling change affects >10% of GPU capacity in a region, automatic rollback trigger is disabled until manual ack.

lucas: I'll own the rollout doc and run canary in eu-west-1 tonight at 02:00 UTC. Will add checklist: preflight (`nvidia-smi -a`, `lsmod | grep nvidia`, kernel version), driver artifact checksum, kubelet/device-plugin path verification, taint/un-taint commands, rollback steps.

mei: Also open a support ticket with cloud provider — there are node images with older kernel-headers that break DKMS installs. Queueing that now.

carla: Cost note — if we keep draining/reshuffling across regions we'll pay cross-zone egress and extra instances. Keep alerting on autoscaler churn.

kevin: Action items: 1) Lucas: canary rollout doc + helm values for driver.enabled. 2) Mei: cloud ticket + list of node images with older kernels. 3) Priya: coordinate with ML teams for paused jobs, provide temporary taint instructions. 4) I'll open PR to pin gpu-operator charts in our infra repo and add rollback playbook.

priya: Thanks — ping me when canary is up and I'll coordinate job holds. :thumbsup:
